title: Aung San Suu Kyi speaks to son after five years in detention in Myanmar
description:
The son of Myanmar's former leader Aung San Suu Kyi said Friday that when he finally got to speak with his mother, who has spent more than five years in detention in the Southeast Asian country, it seemed in some ways like not much time had passed at all.
"She sounds like herself, and still sounds strong," said Kim Aris, adding that her voice was a bit croaky, like she had a cold.
Myanmar's military government on Thursday allowed Aris a 20-minute phone call with his 81-year-old mother, one of the world's most famous political prisoners. He spoke from Myanmar's embassy in London to Suu Kyi in her country's capital, Naypyitaw, where she's serving an 18-year sentence under house arrest.
Suu Kyi has been detained since February 2021, when Myanmar's army ousted her elected government. Held mostly incommunicado, she's serving an 18-year prison term on charges that supporters and rights groups say are bogus and politically inspired.
